paragraphs.source_en: Iroha-hime had naturally wished to bear her husband's first son herself, but a maid she had met only a few times had beaten her to it. She remembered that the woman was the daughter of a country samurai from near Kasugayama. Her name was Okiku; she spoke little, always kept her eyes lowered and head bowed, and had a frail, pitiable air. Iroha-hime had never imagined that Tadateru would take a liking to her, yet she had conceived—and even borne him a son!
